description.describe_ch: 此為財務管理的入門課程，旨在熟悉財務資產評價、資本預算、及公司投資決策等重要課題，學期中需作研究報告，以期將財務理論與實務予以融會貫通。
description.describe_eh: This is an introductory course in the field of financial management. It will provide students with the basic understanding of financial asset valuation and corporate investment decision. Research projects will be assigned to students during the semester. The purpose is to familiarize students with the theories and concepts learned from the class and apply them to the real financial world.
description.pre_subname: ECON1001經濟學(一)、ECON1002經濟學(二)、ACCT1011會計學(一)、ACCT1012會計學(二)

targets.describe_ch: 瞭解財務資產評價、資本預算、公司投資決策、資本結構管理及股利政策
targets.describe_en: Understand the financial asset valuation, the capital budgeting, the corporate investment decision, the capital structure management and the dividend policy

targets.describe_ch: 綜合: 將財務理論與實務予以融會貫通
targets.describe_en: Integrate the Financial Theory with Practice

textBooks.tpb_book:
Contemporary Financial Management, 14th Edition
by
Moyer, McGuigan, and Rao
 
Contemporary Financial Management (CFM), 14e, emphasizes the overriding goal of value creation, and the tools used to manage the assets of an enterprise, optimize sources of financing, control financial risk, recognize the value of real and financial options, and enhance a firm’s cash flows. These skills are learned within the context of abiding by ethical business practices, following sound corporate governance principles, and recognizing the importance of the extensive international dimensions of financial management. CFM 14e is updated to reflect recent real world illustrations of the use of these tools.
textBooks.tpb_book_en: Ross, S. A., Westerfield, R. W., and Jordan, B. D., Fundamentals of Corporate Finance, 14th Edition, 2024, McGraw-Hill. (華泰書局代理).

gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol:
To succeed in this course, follow the guidelines below each week.
•Read the textbook pages listed in the syllabus and found on the weekly assignment pages.
•Read the weekly lecture and any other supporting document provided by the course instructor.
•Work the weekly homework problems, and submit them as required by the instructor.
•Perform the weekly homework exercises.
gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol_en:
Attendance
Please be on time. The professor may ask you to leave if you're late without a good reason.
Don't leave early. It's not acceptable to complete attendance and then leave before class is over.
Return from breaks on time and be ready to continue.
Notify the professor in advance if you cannot attend class for a valid reason, such as illness or an emergency.
During Class
Pay attention. Avoid distractions like playing computer games, listening to music, wearing headphones, or watching movies.
Be respectful. Don't chat with other students while the professor is speaking. It disrupts the class and is disrespectful to the professor and your peers.
Participate actively. You are encouraged to engage in the class discussions.
Let one person speak at a time, including when answering questions.
During Presentations
Be respectful to your classmates. Avoid talking or making noise during presentations.
Listen to the presenter. All group members should avoid talking to each other while one person is presenting.
Stay in the room. Don't walk in or out of the classroom during a presentation unless it's an emergency. Wait until the presentation is finished.
Give constructive feedback and ask questions respectfully when it is appropriate.
gradeRuleDescribe.course_rem:
•Take all quizzes and examinations 
•Participate in the weekly discussions.
•Turn in all work on time.
gradeRuleDescribe.course_rem_en: Success starts with following the class guidelines.
